# Investigation + plan — the MOM footer sentence (app 1.2.3)

Old first sentence:  "Please review and confirm the accuracy of this document."
New first sentence:  "Please review this document and reply with your comments or approval."
The second line stays byte-identical:
"Generated by IHP Project Delivery Platform · Confidential · {date} (PR-{pr_number})".

## 1. Every place the old sentence appears (repo-wide grep, fresh)

~~~
backend/templates/mom_template.html:260   <div class="confirm">Please review and confirm the accuracy of this document.</div>
backend/app/api/mom.py:861                "Please review and confirm the accuracy of this document.\n\n"
backend/tests/test_mom_media.py:95        assert "Please review and confirm the accuracy of this document." in body["html"]
backend/tests/test_mom_media.py:269       assert "Please review and confirm the accuracy of this document." in draft["body"]
PLAN_MOM_LIVE.md:255                      …Please review and confirm the accuracy of this document. Regards…
~~~

* No occurrence in mom_html.py, docgen.py, template_docgen.py, emailer.py or any other service.
* No frontend string: the live preview is an `<iframe srcDoc>` of the server-rendered HTML, so nothing in
  frontend/src holds the footer.
* No test in test_mom_flow.py / test_mom_html.py asserts the old sentence (they assert only the second
  line, test_mom_flow.py:607).
* PLAN_MOM_LIVE.md:255 is a historical plan document quoting the then-current body; it will be updated
  with the same sentence so the repo-wide grep goes to **zero** with no exception needed.
* The second line appears in exactly three places: mom_template.html:261 and the two assertions
  test_mom_flow.py:607 and test_mom_media.py:96 — all three stay untouched.

## 2. The .docx template is binary, and the sentence is not in it

python-docx over backend/templates/mom_template.docx: 9 paragraphs, 4 tables, two section footers.
A scan of every paragraph, every table cell and both section footers for "Please review", "Generated by",
"Confidential" and "confirm the accuracy" returns **no hits**; the section footers are empty strings.

So the Word minute does not carry the footer today: the task is to **add** it, not replace it. The template
stays binary and untouched. Mechanism: **post-process the rendered .docx** with python-docx (already a
dependency) in one small helper, so the footer text lives in code and can be reviewed and tested.

## 3. Which surfaces share one string, which use the .docx template

| Surface | Renderer | Shares the footer string |
|---|---|---|
| /mom/preview | mom_html.render_html(build_html_context(...)) | yes |
| /mom/view | the same call (byte-identical, 1.2.1 guarantee) | yes |
| /mom/export?format=pdf | Chromium prints that same HTML via mom_pdf_file() | yes |
| /mom/email.eml attachment | mom_pdf_file() - literally the export file (1.2.2 guarantee) | yes |
| MOM email HTML body (for_email=True) | the same HTML renderer | yes |
| /mom/export?format=docx, /mom/generate, assistant mom.draft | docxtpl on mom_template.docx (api/mom.py:322, api/mom.py:769, assistant_orchestrator.py:612) | no - separate |

Cache caveat: mom_pdf_file() returns a cached generated/{code}.pdf and _mom_styled_pdf() caches
mom/*_minute.pdf, so a stale footer could survive a template edit. Live disk: one **orphan** cached PDF
(generated/IHP-MOM-PR-12864-R02.pdf - the record is v2, i.e. R01, so nothing references it) plus minute
PDFs for PR-12864 (v1) and PR-12592 (v4).

## 4. PRs with a stored MOM (new text appears on the next render/export)

Live: **3 MOM records** - PR-12718, PR-12592, PR-12864 (292 projects), 3 stored Word minutes on disk.
Nothing stored is edited. /mom/preview, /mom/view, both exports and the .eml pick the new text up
immediately (they render at request time, once the PDF cache guard is in), while
GET /mom/download?format=docx|minute-pdf keeps serving the stored files until the MOM is regenerated.

## 6. Exact mechanism for the Word

~~~python
MOM_FOOTER_CONFIRM = "Please review this document and reply with your comments or approval."
MOM_FOOTER_META = "Generated by IHP Project Delivery Platform · Confidential · {generated_at}"

def render_mom_docx(project, mom, details, out_path: Path) -> Path:
    """The Word minute: the team's .docx template plus the shared footer lines."""
    context = build_mom_context(project, details, mom.version)
    path = docgen.render_docx(MOM_TEMPLATE_NAME, context, out_path)
    from docx import Document as DocxDocument
    document = DocxDocument(str(path))
    document.add_paragraph(MOM_FOOTER_CONFIRM)
    document.add_paragraph(
        MOM_FOOTER_META.format(generated_at=mom_html.generated_at(project.pr_number))
    )
    document.save(str(path))
    return path
~~~

## 7. Tests

1. test_mom_media.py:95 and :269 move to the new sentence and get stricter: new present **and** old absent.
2. New test_mom_footer_sentence_everywhere - a real render asserting, for the HTML (/preview and /view,
   still byte-identical), the HTML handed to the PDF renderer, the exported .docx text (python-docx) and the
   .eml attachment bytes: new sentence present, old sentence absent. The dev box has no Chromium, so the PDF
   is covered there by the captured HTML and by real PDF text extraction in the live run.
3. One test that proves the exported .docx contains the new sentence (python-docx paragraph walk).

## 8. Live verification (verify_mom_media.py, PR-12864 + PR-12592)

* GET /preview -> new in html, old not in html; GET /view -> body equals the preview html.
* GET /export?format=pdf -> pymupdf text: new present, old absent.
* GET /export?format=docx -> python-docx text: new present, old absent.
* GET /email.eml -> attachment bytes equal the export bytes, and its extracted text has the new sentence.
* The restore in the existing finally puts PR-12864 back (details, version, attachments, audit watermark).
* Repo grep for the old sentence must return zero.
